title: `unsafe_allow_html=True` in single-line `st.markdown` breaks `help` parameter.
body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary If the `unsafe_allow_html` parameter is set to `True` in `st.markdown()`, and the contents aren't followed by a double carriage return, then if the `help` parameter is also used, it's rendered as `:help[]` rather than as the actual help icon. This is obviously not helpful. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st # This doesn't work. st.markdown("

an example

", unsafe_allow_html=True, help="test") # This "works" but the help icon is on the next line, not at the end of the first line. st.markdown("""

an example

""", unsafe_allow_html=True, help="test") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce See reproducible code example, repeated here for good measure: 1. Put this in your streamlit file: ``` import streamlit as st st.markdown("

an example

", unsafe_allow_html=True, help="test") ``` 2. Look at rendered output. ### Expected Behavior The help should be rendered as a proper help icon with hover text. I don't want to have to put the help icon on the next line, I want it to be at the end of the one-line block where I put it! ### Current Behavior The above code produces this on the Streamlit page: an example :help[] ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.57 - Python version: 3.14 - Operating System: Windows x64 - Browser: Firefox ### Additional Information _No response_

### Issue Analysis This is a frontend rendering bug in `st.markdown`. When `help` is supplied (and the markdown is not LaTeX or a single badge), the frontend appends a remark text directive marker to the body — i.e. `` `${body} :help[]` `` in [`Markdown.tsx`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/frontend/lib/src/components/elements/Markdown/Markdown.tsx#L77-L94). A custom remark plugin then transforms `:help[]` into the inline help icon, with the actual tooltip text supplied via `HelpTextContext`. The bug occurs because of how CommonMark handles raw HTML: when `unsafe_allow_html=True` and the body starts with block-level HTML on a single line (e.g. `

an example

`), the parser treats the entire line as a raw HTML block. Anything appended on that same line — including the ` :help[]` directive marker — is consumed as part of the HTML block and is never parsed as a text directive, so it leaks through as the literal text `:help[]`. Adding a blank line after the HTML closes the HTML block and lets `:help[]` be parsed as its own paragraph, which is why the workaround in the issue "works" (but at the cost of placing the icon on a new line). A likely fix is to special-case `allowHtml && help` similarly to how the LaTeX case is already handled — render the body via `StreamlitMarkdown` and render an `InlineTooltipIcon` next to it inside `StyledLabelHelpWrapper`, rather than relying on the `:help[]` directive that doesn't survive inside an HTML block. ### Related Issues - [#7371 - Inconsistent display of 'help' in st.markdown](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7371) — Another confirmed bug about `help` rendering inconsistencies in `st.markdown` (visual difference vs. `st.title`); likely overlaps with the same code path in `Markdown.tsx`. - [#6718 - Widget help parameter should accept an html string](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6718) — Related interaction between the `help` parameter and HTML, though the direction is reversed (HTML inside `help`). - [#8322 - Alignment issue with help tooltips inside st.popover](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8322) — A different but adjacent bug about help-tooltip rendering quirks; relevant if a fix touches the shared tooltip/help-icon rendering pipeline. --- *This is an automated triage comment using `claude-opus-4-7-thinking-xhigh`. Please verify the suggested labels and related issues.*
